Iconic Fiat Barchetta Roadster Comes Back to CGI Life Across Imagination Land With Abarth Mod in Tow
7 photos
Photo: augusto_fuchsdesign / Instagram
The Italian automaker Fiat has always been renowned as a specialist in cute little automobiles that showcase the Italian ‘La Dolce Vita’ in affordable, light, and compact packages that can easily dwell around crowded cities.
Their current range is a testament to that: Fiat makes a raft of A- and B-segment models, both passenger cars and crossover SUVs, and very few C- and above models . Their success is not to be underestimated, also: although they mostly have an audience at home on the Old Continent and in Latin America, Fiat remains the most successful brand in the Stellantis portfolio in terms of sales.
They cater to many segments, from the tiny Fiat Topolino quadricycle to the newly introduced Grizzly and Grizzly Fastback, two new C-segment family cars that still measure less than 4.5 meters in length and which had their home gala premiere at the recent 2026 Paris Motor Show – but fans always want more, of course.
Sometimes, they even get their prayers answered, even though only by the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. For example, Augusto Fuchs, aka ' augusto_fuchsdesign ' on social media, is a Transportation Design Master at IED Torino and Surface Modeler and Designer for Airbus Helicopters with a knack for automobiles – in his spare time, most likely.
Recently, they imagined an unofficial, hypothetical design project aimed at bringing back the fancy Mercedes-Benz SLS without the AMG pizzazz but keeping the gullwing doors and instead featuring ample inspiration from the recent Mercedes-Benz Vision Iconic concept for a flagship grand tourer model. But, of course, that one is dedicated to the one percenter fanbase.
Now, he’s back with a new idea: to revive the way more affordable and potentially more fun Fiat Barchetta roadster. The original was produced by Fiat between 1995 and 2005 as an open-top sports car aimed at the same category of clients as the ones purchasing a Mazda MX-5 Miata. It was based on the Fiat Punto, but it had a completely independent style, aimed at referencing both classic roadsters and traditional small skiffs used for recreational purposes.
In his vision, the Fiat Barchetta would come back to life with the same diminutive size but packing modern content like round LED headlights, large LED taillights, and funky aerodynamic wheels. It’s still a petite two-door two-seat sports car, and affordability would be a big part of the package, hence the ICE powertrain hinted at by the dual exhaust outlets tucked into the bumper.
By the way, since the Fiat Barchetta would be tremendously fun to drive, the pixel master also imagined a variant packing the Abarth style and punch – complete with racing stripes, a single larger exhaust tucked inside a proper diffuser, and most likely a more potent engine sitting under the hood. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Augusto_Fuchs design (@augusto_fuchsdesign)

Ford Confirms Another Affordable Truck Is Coming
11 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford has just confirmed the arrival of a new, budget-friendly midsize pickup truck, set to launch in 2027, engineered for international markets rather than the United States. CEO Jim Farley revealed that the unnamed model will feature a base material cost 20% lower than the current Ford Ranger.
This upcoming Ford-badged international pickup truck is entirely different from both the unibody U.S. market Maverick and the upcoming 2027 Ford Fathom , both positioned as Ford’s most affordable pickup trucks.
Ford is well aware that the firm will need to play the ace up its sleeve to better compete with low-cost Chinese automakers. That is exactly why the automaker is making efforts to reduce costs in order to roll out affordable products.
During Ford’s third-quarter earnings call, CEO Jim Farley highlighted the intense price competition in Latin America and Southeast Asia, with Australia also considered a likely candidate given the strong local demand for budget trucks.
Photo: Ford The truck will be designed to replicate the Maverick 's entry-level U.S. success on a global scale. It directly targets affordable Chinese rivals, such as the BYD Shark 6 and the GWM Cannon, which have been making the rules in the segment in the area.
To keep production costs down, Ford could count on its Chinese joint venture with Jiangling Motors, which already produces midsize pickup trucks such as the Yuhu. Unlike the Maverick, the new truck is expected to retain a traditional ladder-frame chassis for work-oriented buyers.
Ford has yet to disclose the exact powertrain that will put its new model in motion, but it is very unlikely to see yet another EV that would bite big chunks of the Fathom's future market share.
The design is also taking shape behind closed doors.
A reduction of 20% in base material costs does not guarantee a 20% lower sticker price, but it gives Ford significant room to undercut the Ranger and allow future Ranger generations to move upmarket. In the meantime, buyers will have more to choose from for less money.
Photo: Ford The Ford Fathom will drop as the second most affordable electric pickup truck, with a starting price of $29,945, with taxes included. In the meantime, the Slate remains the cheapest in the segment, kicking off at $24,950. However, the Slate truck has crank windows, zero screens on board, and no speakers.
This is how Ford is also trying to snatch customers from other auto brands. " This truck is designed to bring new customers into the Ford truck lineup internationally at a cost structure that allows us to compete, in this case, with the Chinese ," Jim Farley explained, as reported to Autoblog.
With the Fathom ready to hit the market next year, Ford will fast-track the new model for a 2027 launch as well, but hasn't revealed the exact date.

Young Man Passed Away, His Dad Kept His SUV. Now, He Sees It Clean for the First Time in 15 Years
16 photos
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube
Fifteen years have passed since Mark lost his son in an accident. His SUV, a Land Rover Range Rover, remained at home, parked, without moving an inch all this time, exposed to the sun and battered by the rain, collecting mold and dust instead of miles. There was a time when the grieving father couldn't even look at it. Now, he called the detailers because he wants to see it clean, up and running again.
This Land Rover Range Rover has sat for too long. It spent years in the woods, under a walnut tree, and then some of his friends agreed to host it. Even though there was a time he couldn’t even stand to look at the SUV, he just couldn’t let it go. It belonged to his youngest son, Cody, who passed away in 2011.
This Range Rover was his Christmas present soon after his 16th birthday. He sure deserved it! With tears in his eyes and his voice trembling, Mark describes his son as a pretty awesome kid and says everybody loved him. " He was good at everything. He’d pick up any sport, and he’d excel at it immediately, " the heartbroken father recalls. He was 18 when he passed. He had just graduated high school when he had an accident, and that was it. Time stood still.
After he lost his son, Mark kept his distance from the young man’s SUV. Then he remembered it brought back good memories and didn’t want to see it neglected anymore. So he called a team of detailers. They arrived at the scene, loaded the Range Rover onto their trailer, and off they went.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube Now, the detailers have to scrub away years of abandonment, during which the SUV collected grime, moss, mold, and dust instead of miles. They start with one single plan: to make it look brand-new again and make it run and drive like it just rolled off the production line, because it is not just about cleaning a car, but bringing a part of the past back to a grieving father.
For starters, they remove the tow bar installed up front and the carrier mounted out back to access every inch of the vehicle. Besides, Mark asked them to. Because the rear carrier is bolted with pins that have rusted over the years, RJ and his team need to cut them off and slide the accessory out. The earth started to claim the Range Rover. Grass grew through the spokes of the wheels with massive 27-millimeter lugs.
The pre-wash removes some of the dirt, but it doesn’t really work miracles on a vehicle abandoned under a walnut tree, exposed to the elements for years and years. But what worries RJ of WD Detailing the most is not the green slime, but the thick baked-on layer of grease that hides underneath it.
That is where the pre-wash cuts in. If the detailers start scrubbing the dirt off, they risk damaging the fragile paint, but the chemicals do the job far better. Afterwards, the foam lifts the remaining grime. RJ starts wet-sanding the paint with an ultra-fine sandpaper, as terrifying as it may seem, even before the actual wash, so that he can get rid of the dirt embedded in the top layer.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube The cabin is just as bad, with the rear bench seat hosting parts, boxes, and the rear hatch, but also junk that goes straight into the trash bin. RJ removes everything to have enough space to clean the interior. He also needs to remove the front seats, but the seat control button that moves them forward and backward no longer works, and he needs to slide the seat forward to reach the rear bolts.
So he puts power directly into the connections and manages to move the seats forward, as the motor is still functional. Now, he can have his way with the carpet, blowing out the dust, vacuuming it out, and agitating the dirt. The hot-water extractor and a drill brush work their magic.
In the meantime, the seats, with a makeshift vinyl seating area, probably hiding severely damaged factory leather upholstery, need a brutal multi-step attack with spraying, scrubbing, steaming, and wiping away the dirt, along with tons of patience.
The vehicle they are working on is a Land Rover Range Rover Classic , a four-door model from the late 1980s or early 1990s, powered by an American engine. But how did GM’s 3.9-liter V8 end up under the hood of the British off-roader?
[fullimg11}
Back in 1961, General Motors introduced a compact, lightweight, all-aluminum 215-cubic-inch (3.5-liter) V8 for the Buick Special, Oldsmobile F-85, and Pontiac Tempest. However, it turned out to be a failure right from the get-go. Aluminum casting technology at the time led to high scrap rates and costly manufacturing, and coolant issues caused by improper antifreeze use led GM to discontinue the engine after the 1963 model year.
In 1965, British carmaker Rover bought the tooling and manufacturing rights from GM after realizing the lightweight aluminum engine was ideal for British sedans and off-roaders. Rover used the original 3.5-liter design for over two decades before enlarging the cylinder bores for the 1990 model year to create the 3.9-liter V8.
The power plant pushes out 182 horsepower (185 metric horsepower) and 220 pound-feet (298 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 11.6 seconds (true, it's not exactly a sporty SUV) and a top speed of 110 mph (177 kph).
Now, this is what the mechanic, Adam, has to bring back to life. He feeds electricity to the V8, and it turns over. However, the fuel pump must have given its last breath a long time ago. He has no spark, either, so here it goes. The nightmare begins.
Photo: WD Detailing | YouTube But Adam is a magician, and hours of hard work and patience to get the parts he ordered eventually pay off. When RJ turns the key in the ignition, and the V8 fires right up, filling the studio with a deep growl and sounding like it longed to hit the road.
The team worked day in and day out to give Mark a reason to smile. That was worth every single minute of scrubbing and rubbing away over a decade of sitting abandoned. " This looks way better than when I bought it, " Mark says.

BMW’s iX4 Gets Its First Tuning Job, Albeit Only Digitally
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
Is the new-gen BMW iX3 a bit too practical for your taste and you want something with less rear headroom and not that much space in the cargo area with a similar design? Well, you’re in luck, because there is also an iX4 that has joined the above-mentioned model.
Unveiled one month ago, it is the third model based on the Neue Klasse platform after the iX3 and i3 Sedan, and it’s all about the Neue Klasse in terms of design, too. That’s because it features the same quirky design as its new-age siblings, as well as the same cockpit layout, complete with the Panoramic iDrive, a 17.9-inch central touchscreen infotainment system, an optional 3D head-up display, Amazon Alexa+ tech for the voice assistant, and many other gizmos.
Topping the lineup will be the iX4 M60 xDrive, which will have 603 horsepower (450 kW/612 ps) and 645 pound-feet (875 Nm) of torque to play with. It is estimated to reach 149 mph (240 kph) flat out, and do 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in 3.7 seconds. An electronically-controlled rear M Sport differential, an Adaptive M suspension, a revised chassis setup, 21-inch wheels offered as standard, and yellow lighting will be on deck, alongside other features. This model will launch sometime next year.
Mind you, it won’t be the only version to launch in 2027, as the same goes for the iX4 50 xDrive. It has a pair of electric motors with xDrive all-wheel drive, and offers 463 hp (345 kW/469 ps) and 475 pound-feet (644 Nm) of torque via the right pedal, enabling 0-60 mph (97 kph) in 4.7 seconds, and a 130 mph (209 kph) top speed. The 112.2 kWh battery enables an estimated range of 428 miles (689 km). The model can charge at up to 400 kW, adding 184 miles (296 km) of range in just 10 minutes.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project Now, it is only a matter of time until we get to see the first real tuning jobs for the BMW iX4 , as there should be plenty of companies offering all kinds of upgrades for this model, though most of them will likely be visual. Meanwhile, though, the electric premium compact crossover coupe is enjoying its first tuning job in Fantasy Land. What do we mean by that? That the build you see above is not real, as it came from @ildar_project and was shared on social media a couple of days ago.
The pixel artist gave this BMW iX4 a widebody kit, which consists of the usual wheel arch attachments that have made the entire thing look a lot more muscular compared to the stock EV. It also features new side skirt attachments, as well as some add-ons at the front, including that sharp-looking splitter that has been virtually attached to the OEM bumper. The front hood also seems to have come from the rendering world, but the yellow daytime running lights haven’t, because these are available straight from the factory.
Besides the aforementioned novelties, this CGI-infused BMW iX4 also sports a tweaked grille, and has a quite large wing at the rear, as well as a new diffuser that is on the big side of things, and sports an extra brake light integrated in the middle. The concave wheels are larger and wider than the OEM ones, and have a V-spoke design, and a silver finish, whereas the rest of the car has a minty look, which is why the rendering artist behind this project calls it the Mint Bullet.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project Now, the work hasn’t ended here, because this BMW iX4 also sits a lot closer to the asphalt, so a lowering kit is part of the virtual tuning job. Due to this mod, and the larger alloys, this thing would be a lot jigglier than the stock one if it were real, but that’s the price to pay for giving any vehicle a similar treatment. On a more positive note, though this thing would corner faster.
The interior hasn’t had its pixels altered, though something like this would need a makeover here, too, in order to stand out from the crowd more. And a lively upholstery would be a must, alongside new trim, some contrast stitching perhaps, a new steering wheel, modified seats, and a renowned tuner’s name displayed on quite a few components.
Now, this virtually-tuned BMW iX4 looks like something that is only a forged carbon look away from resembling something that might come from Mansory’s portfolio, because it is definitely on the flashy side of things, and, between us, it does not feature the most inspiring tuning job. And you can easily see those BMW roundels replaced with the controversial tuner’s emblems, can’t you?
I’m not exactly a fan of this CGI build, but then again, I can’t say I like the iX4 , or other Neue Klasse BMW products. But what’s your take on this modded iX4? Would you see yourself daily driving it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)

2026 SEMA Show • Toyota Brings Fresh Adventure-Ready Concepts at the 2026 SEMA Show Under the Woodland Banner
The Perfect Travel Companion Is a Wonderfully Cozy French Tiny House
29 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
If people were fully satisfied with RVs, trailers, and all kinds of repurposed buses, perhaps there would be no need for tiny homes, but the truth is that everyone longs for that nostalgic feeling of “being at home” even when they’re on the road a lot. A tiny home can bring both of these together – the tender comfort of a traditional living space, and the total freedom of a mobile abode.
Tiny homes are the best thing out there that can serve as an alternative to both conventional houses and standard RVs. Of course, in each case, there are certain downsides, but many people all over the world find tiny homes better than most options. An adequately-sized and properly equipped tiny home can become the perfect travel companion for modern-day adventurers with a wanderlust, while also providing the comforting familiarity of a traditional home layout.
Tiny house Meridionale fits this description perfectly. A typically French compact mobile home with a length of just 5.5 meters (18 feet) and no more than 20 square meters (215 square feet) of floor space overall, Tiny Meridionale is built for the road. At the same time, its charming interior reveals the versatility and playfulness of a bigger and more modern house.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Don’t be fooled by the traditional wooden paneling and compact silhouette – this French house on wheels hides phenomenal functionality, enough to rival a conventional house for four. To top things off, Tiny Meridionale even boasts enhanced autonomy for energy savings and a more sustainable way of living. The fully-equipped version showcased in the gallery includes a complete solar power kit (you can see the solar panels on the roof) and a waterless toilet.
The corrugated metal roof features a gabled section that adds the timeless charm of a classic countryside home, and a single-slope section specifically intended to support the home’s solar panels. The beautiful exterior cladding, free of artificial colors and toxic paint, is entirely Douglas fir sourced from local Occitania woods that are also managed sustainably. Occitania is where Mon Reve en Bois, the builder of Tiny Meridionale, operates.
A somewhat unusual layout is coupled with clever modular furniture to add even better functionality to this small living space. Instead of the central placement that is more often used, the kitchen was moved to one end of the house. That leads to a limited counter space, but other than that, Tiny Meridionale’s kitchen offers surprisingly generous storage.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Take a look at the ingenious shelves carved into the wall, that look more like tiny nooks, but that successfully replace the standard upper cupboards which would have been too bulky for this small area. A couple of traditional lower cupboards provide additional storage under the countertop, and tiny open shelves were also added next to the fridge nook.
The bathroom is located right next to this compact kitchen, featuring a timber door that blends in so seamlessly with the walls that it almost looks invisible. Inside, this small bathroom (which is very common for a classic French tiny house) features furniture that is made to measure in order to fit perfectly and also make the most of the limited floor space. That ultra-compact rectangular sink is unusual by American standards, but it works perfectly with the furniture and the space.
Tiny Meridionale hides several pieces of modular furniture that look as charming and playful as LEGO elements, but have a very practical purpose. In the kitchen, an ultra-slim console near the main entrance hides 3in1 functionality, with storage and display space on top, built-in tiny drawers at one end, and a large foldable extension that becomes a big dining table.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois In the lounge, you’ll also discover four little cabinets with pigeon-hole drawers that boast incredible versatility. They can be combined in the form of a modern coffee table for the lounge or stacked to create one, big storage unit with multiple drawers. When used separately, two sets of each can serve as perfect night stands for the lounge (which is meant to double as a ground-floor bedroom) and for the loft.
Owners get to decide how they prefer to use these modular cabinets, and they’re free to play around with all the options. The lounge itself was specifically intended for better flexibility. If furnished with a convertible sofa, it can be easily turned into a second bedroom by night, but there’s also the option of two cozy armchairs instead, for a classic lounge ambiance (you can see both options featured in the gallery).
Either way, this lounge feels spacious and cozy at the same time. It lacks the stunning views provided by the oversized picture windows of so many tiny homes these days, but it does have classic windows that bring in sufficient natural light and a beautiful view. For even more storage space, the builder carved shelves in the seating area, creating something that looks a bit like a nook, but without taking too much floor space.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The staircase placement and even an added curtain can provide full privacy for this lounge, especially when it’s used as a second bedroom. It’s a great alternative to actually closing this space with a door, since it also allows for a wider, open space that can be used for other purposes or simply to add that feeling of spaciousness.
The staircase is a hybrid design with asymmetrical treads sometimes referred to as a duck-step staircase. It’s usually preferred in compact living spaces, such as this one, and Tiny Meridionale makes it extra stylish by painting the treads in a contrasting, darker color. Surprisingly, there was no built-in storage added to this staircase, since there are so many other options both in the lounge and the kitchen.
Its only purpose is to connect the loft, which serves as the main bedroom, to the ground floor. Beauty is in the details, and Tiny Meridionale has plenty. Its loft bedroom is elegantly hidden behind a solid timber wall that ensures full privacy, as well as safety. On the inside, this safety wall becomes a practical cabinet with multiple open shelves for both storage and decorative display.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The room itself is surprisingly spacious for such a compact house, meaning that it fits a double bed with comfortable walk-around space, plus nightstands on each side. With pure timber paneling throughout, this bedroom has the ambiance of a lovely cabin in the woods, a perfect place to relax and reconnect with nature. It only lacks the large windows of modern tiny house lofts, but a charming little porthole right above the bed makes up for that.
Welcoming enough for four guests, and fully-equipped even for long-term accommodation, this French tiny house is meant to literally feel like home on the road. Its clever layout demonstrates a wise use of space with a focus on practicality, but tiny details throughout take it from basic to charming. Bespoke modular pieces of furniture are like the cherry on top, allowing owners to have more options and to play with different setups with no need for extra floor space.
The Occitania-based Mon Reve en Bois also makes tiny homes on wheels that are slightly bigger and that can accommodate more people, but Tiny Meridionale is a perfect example of how much can be achieved even within a little over 200 square feet. Full mobility shouldn’t mean sacrificing comfort nor style, and this French tiny house proves it.

2026 SEMA Show • Stellantis Uses Direct Connection to Unleash No Less Than Six New HEMI V8 Crate Engine Packages
Rendering: Lost But Not Forgotten, Rover SD1 Comes Back to Life in CGI As a High-Tech Fastback Sedan
10 photos
Photo: mike.g.concepts / Instagram
There has been a lot of talk about Jaguar Land Rover as of late: the Jaguar reinvention has become real with the Type 01 all-electric high-performance fastback limousine, and Land Rover continues its success story with a ton of novelties, including the all-electric Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, or the previewed Range Rover GT.
Land Rover is incredibly busy, actually. Aside from the three EV models mentioned above, their Land Rover Classic division completely reworked the traditional Defender 90 and 110 models from before the modern L663 iteration and even strapped a 405-hp V8 engine to their upgraded chassis, suspension, and brakes. That’s among a bevy of special editions and the Stellantis agreement to make Land Rovers in the US soon, by the way.
Of course, the most interesting piece of news regarding Land Rover is their desire to break conventions in a manner that’s not unlike the use case of the Jaguar Type 01 – their upcoming Range Rover GT is a completely new body style for the specialty brand that is less of an SUV than ever. As the name implies, it’s a grand tourer that abandons the classic SUV or modern crossover shape in favor of a sleeker fastback body style.
It will ultimately replace both the Range Rover Evoque and Velar models as Land Rover moves the Range Rover series even further upscale, making it also more expensive in the process, but the real shocker is how close it comes to bringing back the spirit of the British automotive brand that, for over a century between 1904 and 2005, used to be Land Rover’s passenger car counterpart instead of Jaguar.
The historic Rover marque had many owners, including the Rover Company, Leyland Motors, British Leyland, the Rover Group, BMW, and JLR since 2013. Currently defunct, Rover probably won’t make it back to the road anytime soon given the upcoming electric and hybrid Range Rover GT – but that hasn’t stopped people from dreaming.
For example, here’s an idea stemming from across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators: Mike G., the leader of the ' mike.g.concepts ' design studio, "fueled by adrenaline and innovation," has reworked the defunct Rover brand back into a virtual lifestyle.
The virtual artist, who knows that Rover went belly up back in 2005, says its legendary design style remains “timeless” even today and, in his opinion, “the boldest and most innovative creation they ever made was the unforgettable SD1,” an executive car produced by British Leyland (BL) from 1976 until 1986 under the Rover nameplate.
His recent unofficial, hypothetical design project now seeks to resurrect the Rover SD1 with modern cues – the still-futuristic lines from the late 1970s have been ‘updated’ for the modern age, “pairing its avant-garde fastback styling with a clean, high-performance electric powertrain” because “some legends deserve a second chapter.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mike G.
